articles.title: A Huge and Powerful New Simulation Helps Explain the Universe's Reionization
articles.description: Cosmologists have another powerful simulation to work with. Lumina is the one of the largest and most detailed cosmological simulations yet and runs on the Frontier supercomputer. It's larger and more detailed than Illustris TNG.
articles.summary: The Lumina simulation, one of the largest and most detailed cosmological models ever created, provides breakthrough insights into the Universe's reionization period.

articles.title: Smithsonian scientists just recreated the first 2 billion years of the Universe
articles.description: Scientists have created one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe ever made, offering an extraordinary new glimpse into the cosmos shortly after the Big Bang. Called Lumina, the groundbreaking simulation recreates the universe’s first 2 billion years, showing how dark matter, gas, and radiation interacted to give rise to the earliest stars, galaxies, and black holes.
articles.summary: Scientists create one of the largest and most detailed simulations of the early universe, modeling the first 2 billion years and advancing our understanding of cosmic origins.

articles.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
articles.description: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy. Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away. One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.
articles.summary: Astronomers discover three actively feeding black holes in a single galaxy from the dawn of time over 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing unexpected early-universe complexity.

articles.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
articles.description: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System. Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star. The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.
articles.summary: Astronomers present evidence for what may be the first moon ever detected beyond our solar system, marking a landmark discovery in exoplanet science.

articles.title: Nasa beschleunigt Mondpläne: Landung 2028, Mondbasis ab Jahresende
articles.description: Die Nasa hält an einer bemannten Mondlandung im Jahr 2028 fest und ändert dafür die Architektur des Artemis-Programms. Ein Überblick.
articles.summary: NASA accelerates its lunar ambitions with plans for a crewed Moon landing in 2028 and establishing a lunar base by year-end, representing a major milestone for the Artemis program.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to Crew Completion of Yearlong Mars Simulation
articles.description: The four volunteers who lived and worked in a simulated NASA Mars mission for more than a year will exit their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health and performance data collected from the simulation can help NASA develop methods […]
articles.summary: NASA's yearlong Mars simulation concludes as four volunteers complete their mission, providing valuable data for future human Mars exploration. This landmark analog mission demonstrates the feasibility and challenges of long-duration crewed missions to the Red Planet.

articles.title: NASA’s Neo Surveyor Sunshade
articles.description: A technician inspects the large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor mission in this image released on Oct. 26, 2026. The sunshade structure, which stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base, will keep the infrared space telescope cool as it searches for near-Earth asteroids and […]
articles.summary: NASA's NEO Surveyor mission undergoes sunshade inspection, a critical component for detecting near-Earth objects. This mission represents a major advancement in planetary defense and asteroid discovery capabilities.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Offers Clues to Protect Crews From Mars Dust
articles.description: Over 1,645 Martian days, NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover measured the fine and ultrafine Martian dust particles found clinging to samples of spacesuit materials that are carried aboard the rover, including some that are small enough to penetrate the lungs and enter the bloodstream. The findings will be published Tuesday, Oct. 27, in the Proceedings of […]
articles.summary: Perseverance rover's long-term dust measurements provide critical insights into Martian dust hazards for future human missions. This data is essential for protecting astronauts and equipment during crewed Mars exploration.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launches toward Phobos in a groundbreaking endeavor to explore Mars' mysterious moon. This mission promises to unlock secrets about the origins and composition of the Martian moon system.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years in space as it continues its groundbreaking mission to study Mercury. This milestone honors the international collaboration advancing our knowledge of the solar system's innermost planet.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional observational capabilities. This discovery highlights the telescope's potential for detecting solar system bodies.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is prepared for launch on an H3 rocket to study Phobos and Deimos. This ambitious international mission will provide unprecedented data about Mars' intriguing moon system.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: Solar Orbiter investigates mysterious magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, revealing new insights into solar dynamics and space weather. This groundbreaking research advances our understanding of the Sun's influence on the inner solar system.

articles.title: Massive Stellar Collisions Could Explain Early Supermassive Black Holes
articles.description: Dense stellar environments were common in the early Universe. These environments fostered more numerous stellar collisions, and some of those would've been mergers that formed very massive stars. Those stars would've exploded as supernovae, becoming massive black holes, the potential seeds for today's supermassive black holes.
articles.summary: Dense stellar collisions in the early Universe may explain the rapid formation of supermassive black holes that were previously difficult to account for.

articles.title: This Oddbal Reflective Lava World is Challenging to Understand
articles.description: Exoplanets extremely close to their stars are expected to have lost their atmospheres. But one of them, TOI-561 b, seems to have a thick atmosphere. Understanding how this super-Earth has an atmosphere is challenging.
articles.summary: The exoplanet TOI-561 b defies expectations by retaining its atmosphere despite being extremely close to its star, challenging current atmospheric models.

articles.title: Hubble Will Give the Roman Space Telescope a Helping Hand
articles.description: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will use gravitational microlensing to study dark matter. But it's a wide-field survey telescope, and the venerable Hubble Space Telescope can do things it can't do. That's why the Hubble is lending a hand.
articles.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will partner with Hubble to use gravitational microlensing as a powerful tool for dark matter studies.

articles.title: Double debris disk orbiting a dead star hints at our solar system's future
articles.description: Astronomers using the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (ESO's VLT) have found a rare disk of debris around a dead star that provides a glimpse of what may happen to our solar system. Unlike in similar systems previously found, the debris—the leftovers of planets that once orbited the star—is organized in a double disk, the two parts separated by a clear gap. The disk appears to be shaped by two planetary bodies, one possibly as big as Pluto, that have survived the violent death of the star.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A rare double debris disk orbiting a white dwarf offers astronomers a glimpse into what our solar system may look like in the distant future.

articles.title: First light: Hera resolves two asteroids instead of one
articles.description: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft for planetary defense has resolved its two target asteroids separately for the first time, revealing the binary nature of the Didymos system, currently some 197 million km (122 million miles) away from Earth.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: ESA's Hera spacecraft achieves first light by successfully resolving two target asteroids separately, advancing planetary defense capabilities.

articles.title: Radio images reveal disturbances from Betelgeuse's mysterious companion that lurks within its shadows
articles.description: The well-known star Betelgeuse has a mysterious houseguest—and it's shaking the rafters, rattling the pipes and slamming the cupboards (metaphorically speaking). It's causing enough subtle atmospheric disturbance that it might as well be making ghost noises. Who's to blame? New data suggest that its recently discovered companion star, Siwarha, is the one doing the haunting.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Radio observations reveal a mysterious stellar companion to Betelgeuse whose gravitational influence creates detectable disturbances in the red supergiant's atmosphere.

articles.title: Webb links interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS to worlds beyond Neptune through similar ice signatures
articles.description: A Southwest Research Institute–led study used NASA's James Webb Space Telescope to examine ice grains streaming from interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, just the third object from beyond our solar system ever identified. The observations point to tiny aggregates of water ice and dust, about a micron or smaller.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope reveals that an interstellar comet shares ice signatures with worlds beyond Neptune, linking our solar system to the broader cosmos.

articles.title: James Webb discovers a scorching lava planet with a “giant sunscreen”
articles.description: A scorching lava planet 280 light-years away has surprised astronomers by apparently maintaining a thick atmosphere despite conditions that should have stripped it away billions of years ago. James Webb Space Telescope observations suggest that TOI-561 b reflects about 75% of incoming starlight, possibly because of mineral clouds that act like a giant sunscreen. The planet may also be continually replenishing its atmosphere through gases released from a global ocean of molten rock.
articles.summary: A scorching lava planet 280 light-years away defies expectations by maintaining a thick atmosphere despite extreme temperatures, challenging planetary science models.

articles.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
articles.description: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed. New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
articles.summary: Samples from NASA's asteroid Bennu mission reveal 4.5-billion-year-old secrets that are rewriting our understanding of how our solar system formed.

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars has uncovered new evidence that dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe’s expansion, may change over time. The findings challenge a cornerstone of modern cosmology and could reshape our understanding of how the universe works.
articles.summary: A massive analysis of 2,884 exploding stars provides new evidence about dark energy and the nature of cosmic acceleration.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Joins the Search for Alien Civilizations
articles.description: Saudi Arabia is joining the search for alien signals coming from the cosmos. They're collaborating with SETI in the endeavour. SETI has announced that two LaserSETI instruments will be positioned in Saudi Arabia, adding to a growing network of optical sensors…
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia joins the international effort to detect signals from extraterrestrial civilizations through collaboration with SETI, expanding the global search for alien life.

articles.title: Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? [8:42]
articles.description: A leading theory proposes that ancient Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours. Space Mysteries: Did a planet-sized object collide with Earth to form the moon? | 8:42 VideoFr…
articles.summary: Leading scientific theories propose that a giant impact between Earth and a planet-sized object created the Moon, reshaping our understanding of the early solar system.

articles.title: NASA JPL Looks to Next 90 Years of Innovation, Exploration
articles.description: Interstellar probes. Lunar drones. Helicopters on Mars. When a group of Caltech graduate students and enthusiasts began conducting rocket-propulsion tests in Pasadena’s Arroyo Seco on Oct. 31, 1936, they had no idea that their work marked the inception of the…
articles.summary: NASA JPL envisions innovative future technologies including interstellar probes, lunar drones, and Martian helicopters as it looks toward the next 90 years of exploration.

articles.title: Achievement Unlocked: Microblazar Confirmed
articles.description: Researchers have confirmed the existence of the first microblazar. Unlike blazars, which are extragalctic and powered by supermassive black holes, microblazars are inside the Milky Way, and are powered by stellar mass black holes. The microblazar may be the s…
articles.summary: Researchers confirm the first discovery of a microblazar, a smaller cosmic object that challenges existing understanding of blazars and high-energy phenomena in the universe.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Views Dust at Neretva Vallis
articles.description: Description This 360-degree look at Neretva Vallis within Mars’ Jezero Crater was stitched together using 217 images acquired by the rover’s Mastcam-Z on May 20, 2024, the 1,155th Martian day, or sol, of the mission. While it is a wind-swept dusty vista today, billions of years ago it was home to a river channel that fed fresh water into […]
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover captures a 360-degree panorama of Neretva Vallis within Jezero Crater, revealing the geological features of this ancient river delta. This imagery advances our understanding of Mars' past habitability.

articles.title: NEO Surveyor’s Sunshade Gets Inspected
articles.description: Description The large sunshade of NASA’s Near-Earth Object (NEO) Surveyor is mounted on an assembly ring during inspections in a clean room at BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems in Boulder, Colorado, in July 2026.  The sunshade structure stands 20 feet (6 meters) tall and measures 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide at its base. Its two flat […]
articles.summary: NEO Surveyor's sunshade undergoes assembly and inspection as the mission advances toward deployment. This crucial technology will enhance our ability to discover and track potentially hazardous asteroids.

articles.title: Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.description:
Image:
			Stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
articles.summary: A spectacular nebular region showcases the dynamic process of star formation within a cosmic cauldron of gas and dust. This imagery reveals the beautiful complexity of stellar birth in our universe.
